steps.user_message:
Here is my medical report, can you analyze it and tell me when I need to see the doctor next? 

Patient Name: Vince Kamniski
DOB: 14 March 1990
Report Date: 28 November 2025
Provider: Dr. Elena Moretti, MD, 
Doctor's Email: moretti@northshoregeneral.com
Clinic: North Shore General Internal Medicine

Reason for Visit: Annual physical examination and routine health screening.

Medical History: Past medical history includes mild seasonal allergic rhinitis and a remote ankle sprain (2021, resolved). No past surgeries. Medications include Loratadine 10 mg as needed. No known drug allergies. Family history: father with hypertension (age 52), mother with hypothyroidism.

Social History: Software engineer. Non-smoker. Alcohol: 2–4 drinks per week socially. Exercises 3–4 times per week (running and weight training). Balanced diet with moderate red-meat intake. Sleep averages 6.5–7 hours nightly.

Vital Signs: Blood Pressure 118/76 mmHg; Heart Rate 68 bpm; Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min; Temperature 36.6°C; Height 181 cm; Weight 83 kg; BMI 25.3.

Physical Examination: Well-appearing male, no acute distress. Cardiovascular: normal S1/S2, no murmurs. Lungs: clear bilaterally. Abdomen: soft, non-tender. Neurological: alert and oriented, normal strength and reflexes. Musculoskeletal: full range of motion. Skin: no suspicious lesions.

Laboratory Results: CBC within normal limits (WBC 5.8, Hemoglobin 15.2 g/dL, Platelets 245). Metabolic panel normal (Sodium 140, Potassium 4.2, Creatinine 0.98 mg/dL, eGFR 104, AST 22, ALT 26). Lipid panel: Total Cholesterol 191 mg/dL, LDL 118 mg/dL, HDL 54 mg/dL, Triglycerides 112 mg/dL. HbA1c 5.2%.

Assessment: Generally healthy adult male. LDL cholesterol slightly elevated. Allergic rhinitis stable.

Plan: Continue regular exercise. Increase dietary fiber, reduce saturated fats to target LDL <100 mg/dL. Recommend dermatology screening every 2 years. Continue Loratadine as needed. Follow up annually.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should analyze the medical report and decide whether the user needs to visit the doctor soon or not
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — this report looks overall reassuring. Below is a brief analysis plus clear recommendations on when to see the doctor next.

Key findings
- Overall health: normal exam and labs; vitals fine.
- Glucose control: HbA1c 5.2% — normal.
- Kidney/liver: within normal limits.
- Lipids: total cholesterol 191 mg/dL, LDL 118 mg/dL — mildly elevated LDL.
- Allergic rhinitis: stable.
- Plan in report: lifestyle changes to target LDL <100 mg/dL, dermatology screening every 2 years, and “follow up annually.”

Recommended follow-up schedule
- Primary care (routine): Annual follow-up as noted in the report — next visit due around 28 Nov 2026 (one year from the report date).
- Lipid recheck: Recheck fasting lipid panel 3 months after starting the recommended diet/exercise changes to see if LDL is improving (around late Feb 2026). If LDL is trending down but not yet <100, re-evaluate at 6 months; if it’s unchanged or rises, discuss medication options with your doctor sooner.
- Dermatology skin check: Every 2 years per the report — next due around 28 Nov 2027.
- Ongoing monitoring: Blood pressure and general health can be checked yearly at the primary care visit unless symptoms arise.

When to see the doctor sooner
- New concerning symptoms: chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, new neurologic symptoms, unexplained weight loss, or new lumps/skin changes — seek care promptly.
- If you want a faster lipid evaluation or are considering medication (statin) now, contact Dr. Moretti to discuss sooner than 3 months.
- If you start any new medication or have changes in health (e.g., new diagnosis, significant weight change), schedule earlier follow-up.

Suggested tests to order at next / interim visits
- Fasting lipid panel (3 months after lifestyle changes)
- Repeat basic metabolic panel and CBC at annual visit (already normal but routine)
- Any additional tests based on symptoms or family history as advised by your physician

Other preventive notes (age 35)
- Colon cancer screening usually begins at 45 (per current USPSTF guidance) — plan to start screening at age 45 unless you have other risk factors.
- Stay up to date on routine vaccines (influenza yearly, tetanus boosters as needed, COVID boosters per current guidance).

Next steps I can help with
- Draft or send a message to Dr. Moretti requesting a lipid panel to be ordered for ~3 months from now.
- Schedule or draft a request for the annual follow-up.
- Summarize this plan into a short message you can save or send.

Disclaimer: I’m not a clinician. This is an interpretation of the report and general guidance — follow Dr. Moretti’s recommendations or contact her for personalized medical advice.
